title: Module review
subtitle: Everything from Germany, Austria and Hungary

steps.prompt: Order these Prädikat levels from least to most ripe.
steps.explanation: Each level demands riper grapes at harvest.

steps.prompt: Match each term to its country or region.
steps.explanation: Each place has its own vocabulary.

steps.prompt: Trocken on a German label means the wine is dry.
steps.explanation: Yes. Trocken allows up to 9 g/l of sugar, usually balanced by acidity.

steps.prompt: Which is Austria's most planted white grape?
steps.explanation: Grüner Veltliner is Austria's signature and most planted grape.

steps.prompt: Since 2013, Tokaji Aszú must contain at least ____ g/l of sugar.
steps.explanation: 120 g/l, equal to the old 5 puttonyos.

steps.title: What you learned
points: German Prädikats show ripeness; trocken means dry
The Mosel is light and steep; the Rhine fuller and drier
Austria's Wachau terms grade dry wines by alcohol
Tokaj's Aszú is one of the world's oldest classified sweet wines
